newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed at their highest levels in two weeks as a resolution of the row between the German government and the Bundesbank over the revaluation of gold reserves sent German Bund futures surging.
Dealers said activity in guilder paper after the German deal was announced was busier than in recent times, with maturities between 2000 and 2002 particularly in demand.

Under the compromise, the German government will reap the profits of the gold revaluation in 1998, rather than 1997 as originally planned, forcing it to find other ways to fill a budget gap and thereby qualify for a single European currency.
"Obviously, the market has heaved a huge sigh of relief," said one London-based trader.
Dealers said the German news contributed to short covering in Bund futures, which fuelled their rally.
One dealer said U.S. hedge funds had been heavy sellers of the futures contract two weeks ago as controversy over the gold revaluation proposal erupted.
He also saw activity across the guilder yield curve as short sellers bought back their positions.
The trader said he saw extension trades with 2000 bonds being exchanged for those maturing in 2002.

He also noted that 1998 Dutch bonds had been under pressure, adding that the squeeze on holders of short positions was solely responsible for the price movement. "I don't think it's been new buying," he said.
Dealers said a 1.0 billion guilder bond from Finland issued in the morning was well received, selling quickly mainly to Dutch institutions looking to invest growing cash piles.
It follows a steady stream of guilder Eurobonds in recent weeks by issuers exploiting the low borrowing requirement of the Dutch government.
